title: Node-separation decay is arithmetically dead; hitbox-disjoint invariant unenforceable
evidence:
+const MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD := 0.25 # keeps node hitboxes (r 0.95) from overlapping
+const MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR := 0.25 # fallback keeps at least 25% of the separation
+		var sep := MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR * (1.0 - float(attempt) / 80.0) * MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD
+		if sep < MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25:
+			sep = MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25
+- 33 connectables (6 routers + 27 houses), separation floor keeps hitboxes disjoint
detail: sep(0)=0.25*0.25=0.0625 equals the floor; every attempt clamps to a constant 0.0625 rad (~0.5 units at R=8). The decay is dead code and r=0.95 hitboxes (need ~0.2375 rad) can overlap despite the spec claim.
recommended_fix: Use sep := MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * (1.0 - attempt/80.0) with floor MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR * MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD, so separation starts at 0.25 rad and actually decays.

title: Placement fallback loop checks one fixed point ten times, then returns it regardless
evidence:
+	var fallback := _from_lon_lat(start + span * 0.5, deg_to_rad(rng.randf_range(-40.0, 40.0)))
+	for attempt in 10:
+		var ok := true
+		for q in placed:
+			if Geodesic.arc_angle(fallback, q) < MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.5:
+				ok = false
+				break
+		if ok:
+			return fallback
+	return fallback
detail: fallback is computed once outside the loop; the ten iterations re-check the identical point, and the unconditional final return ignores the check anyway. The '10 more tries' honoring separation is ornamental — nothing varies per attempt.
recommended_fix: Recompute a new deterministic candidate per attempt (e.g., vary latitude), or delete the loop and return the single fallback directly.

title: draw_end leaves _last_preview_end stale (draw_cancel resets it) — next preview can stay invisible
evidence:
+	_source = null
+	_snap_target = null
+	_preview.visible = false
+
+
+## Focus-loss / system cancel: drop the gesture without committing.
+func draw_cancel() -> void:
+	_source = null
+	_snap_target = null
+	_preview.visible = false
+	_last_preview_end = Vector3.INF
detail: draw_end hides the preview but never resets _last_preview_end; draw_cancel does. A new draw whose first moved endpoint lands within 1e-4 of the previous gesture's last endpoint skips the rebuild and the preview stays invisible.
recommended_fix: Reset _last_preview_end = Vector3.INF in draw_end (or draw_begin) so both exit paths leave identical state.

title: draw_end commits to last move's snap target; release point never re-snapped
evidence:
+func draw_end(screen_pos: Vector2) -> void:
+	if _project_pointer(screen_pos) == Vector3.INF:
+		_snap_target = null
detail: Commit trusts _snap_target from the last motion event; the release re-projection only nulls it over sky. A release on land whose position produced no motion event can commit to a stale target far from the pointer.
recommended_fix: Recompute Geodesic.snap_candidate at the release projection before committing instead of reusing the last move's target.

title: orbit_started signal emitted but never connected
detail: orbit_started is declared and emitted in _begin for ORBIT mode, yet main.gd connects every other router signal except this one. Nothing in the diff consumes it — dead signal.
recommended_fix: Delete the signal and its emit, or connect it to whatever needs orbit-gesture start notification.

title: _arc_mid scales an already-radius-length vector by PLANET_RADIUS again
evidence:
+	var mid := Geodesic.geodesic_points(a.global_position, b.global_position, 2)[1]
+	return mid * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS
detail: geodesic_points already returns points at radius |a| (~8.08 here); multiplying by PLANET_RADIUS again yields a point ~65 units out. Every current caller normalizes, masking the error; the result is not the surface midpoint implied.
recommended_fix: Return mid (already at surface radius) or mid.normalized() * PLANET_RADIUS.

title: Capture 02 comment describes nearest-neighbor framing; code uses 0.65-rad pair
evidence:
+	# 2 — district working altitude: frame between the first node and its
+	# nearest neighbor so the view is oblique (roofs + terrain, ref f2 style).
+	var near_pair := _readable_pair(sites)
detail: The comment promises framing between the first node and its nearest neighbor; _readable_pair actually returns the pair whose span is closest to 0.65 rad. One of them is stale.
recommended_fix: Update the comment to describe the 0.65-rad target pair, or implement nearest-neighbor selection.

title: Capture 01 uses the normalized-sum trick the same file flags as degenerate — on the most-spread pair
evidence:
+	var spread := _most_spread_pair(sites)
+	var frame_p: Vector3 = ((spread[0] as Node3D).global_position + (spread[1] as Node3D).global_position) * 0.5
...same file:
+## Midpoint direction of the geodesic between two sites (antipodal-safe:
+## the normalized-sum trick degenerates for opposite pairs).
detail: _arc_mid's docstring states the normalized-sum trick degenerates for opposite pairs, yet capture 01 frames using exactly that sum on the pair selected for maximal angular separation — the most antipodal-ish pair available. No zero-length guard.
recommended_fix: Use _arc_mid(spread[0], spread[1]) for the globe framing, consistent with the other captures.

title: 'no Sim autoload' check queries a nonexistent setting and always passes
evidence:
+	var project_sim: Variant = ProjectSettings.get_setting("autoload", {})
+	check(project_sim == null or (project_sim as Dictionary).is_empty() or not (project_sim as Dictionary).has("Sim"), "no Sim autoload registered")
detail: Autoloads register as 'autoload/<Name>'; no setting named plain 'autoload' exists, so get_setting returns the default {} and the check passes even with a Sim autoload present. The contract is vacuous.
recommended_fix: Enumerate ProjectSettings keys with prefix 'autoload/' and assert none is named Sim.

title: Spec status 'done' with verification task A3 unchecked
evidence:
+status: 'done'
+- [ ] Godot MCP loop: `lsp-diagnostics` clean on all GDScript; `editor-run` + `debug-output` boot check, iterate on errors -- A3
detail: The frontmatter declares status done while A3 — the task covering the lsp-diagnostics and boot-check acceptance criteria — remains unchecked. The spec contradicts itself about whether verification ran.

title: Merged-bundle radius grows unbounded; only strands are capped
detail: Strands are capped with mini(3*count, 9) but the radius factor 1.0+0.45*(count-1) grows without bound; each extra parallel pipe also raises the elevation. The 'capped' growth docstring only holds for strands.
recommended_fix: Clamp the radius factor too, e.g. minf(1.0 + 0.45 * (count - 1), 2.5).

title: 'same geodesic path' test checks only endpoints while elevation scales with bundle size
evidence:
+	check(vapprox(arc._a, a.global_position, 1e-5) and vapprox(arc._b, b.global_position, 1e-5), "merged bundle keeps the same geodesic path")
...pipe_arc.gd:
+	var path := Geodesic.elevated_path(_a, _b, WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS, BASE_ELEVATION_FRAC * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS * _radius_scale, SEGMENTS)
detail: The 'same geodesic path' assertion checks only endpoints, which never change by construction; meanwhile the merged rebuild scales elevation by _radius_scale, so the bundle's mid-arc path genuinely rises and the test never samples it.
recommended_fix: Sample mid-path points of the merged build, or stop scaling elevation with radius_scale.

title: Cloud puff offset salt omits cloud index — all four clouds share one layout
detail: Salt 45000+puff omits cloud index i that the neighboring 41000/42000/43000/44000 draws all include, so every cloud gets identical puff x/y offsets; only radii differ. Reads as a copy-paste miss, not per-cloud seeding.
recommended_fix: Use 45000 + i * 10 + puff, matching the radius salt pattern.

title: Spec matrix promises pinch zoom; only mouse wheel is handled
evidence:
+| Zoom ladder | Scroll/pinch | Altitude eases between globe/district/street stops (damped), never continuous drift | N/A |
...input_router.gd:
+	if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.pressed \
+			and (event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP or event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN):
detail: The spec's edge matrix promises Scroll/pinch zoom; the router only maps MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP/DOWN. InputEventMagnifyGesture and trackpad pan are unhandled, so pinch does nothing.
recommended_fix: Handle InputEventMagnifyGesture (threshold → zoom step) or amend the matrix row to scroll-only.

title: _deterministic_perp docstring claims 'least aligned' axis; code only avoids the dominant one
evidence:
+## Deterministic for parallel and antipodal inputs: picks the world axis
+## least aligned with `a` (X, then Y, then Z) crossed with a.
...body:
+	var ax := Vector3.AXIS_X
+	if absf(ua.x) >= absf(ua.y) and absf(ua.x) >= absf(ua.z):
+		ax = Vector3.AXIS_Y
+	elif absf(ua.y) >= absf(ua.x) and absf(ua.y) >= absf(ua.z):
+		ax = Vector3.AXIS_Z
detail: Docstring claims the axis 'least aligned' with a is picked; the code merely avoids the dominant axis (Z-dominant input falls through to X even when Y is less aligned). Result stays perpendicular, the description is wrong.
recommended_fix: Rephrase the docstring to 'a world axis not dominant in a', or implement true least-aligned selection.

title: World seed 20260904 duplicated as bare literals in test_no_sim
evidence:
+const SEED := 20260904 # slice-1 world seed — deterministic from here
...test_no_sim.gd:
+		biomes[WorldSeed.biome_at(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(20260904), 20260904, s.surface_pos)] = true
detail: The world seed is hardcoded in main.gd as SEED and again as bare literals throughout test_no_sim. Change the seed in one place and the biome/determinism checks silently test a world the game no longer builds.
recommended_fix: Reference Main.SEED (or a shared constant) from the tests instead of repeating 20260904.
